name: Brisklund Wheat Price Assurance Act

source_sentences: A deficiency payment is paid to the holder (the person registered as farming the land) of each registered farm.
The payment rate is Th 220 less the national average farm-gate price for the marketing year, when that price is below Th 220; otherwise zero.
It is paid in December after the marketing year.
The payments are funded as follows: "Such sums as are needed for payments under this Act shall be paid out of the Consolidated Fund."
The Ministry of Agriculture's payments office administers the claims on the Farm Register, at a cost of about Th 4 million a year from its general appropriation.
Harvest declarations are checked by sampling (about 3% of farms a year); false declarations are subject to repayment and a fine of up to twice the payment.
The bill was introduced with the government's majority on 10 February 2027 and enacted on 30 June 2027.
It covers the crop years 2028 to 2032 (the harvests of those years; winter wheat for 2028 is sown in autumn 2027).
Parliament must review the target price before 2032.

unclear.text: Whether the payment is made on each farm's actual output (the harvest declared for the crop year) or on a fixed historical base (its established production).
readings: U1-a: the payment is on the harvest declared for the crop year (actual output)
U1-b: the payment is on the farm's established production, the crop year fixing only the year whose price sets the rate

context: About 18,000 farms grow wheat on about 570,000 hectares; at about 7.0 tonnes a hectare they produce about 4.0 million tonnes a year.
About 2.5 million tonnes are used at home (1.4 by millers, 1.1 as animal feed) and about 1.5 million tonnes are exported.
World wheat production is about 800 million tonnes and world trade about 200 million; Brisklund's exports are under 1% of world trade.
The farm-gate price follows the export price less freight.

Over the past ten marketing years the national average farm-gate price ranged from Th 175 to Th 285 a tonne, averaged about Th 232, and was below Th 220 in four of the ten years, by about Th 20 on average in those years.
About 40% of wheat land is rented, on leases of three to five years; wheat land sells for about Th 12,000 a hectare and rents for about Th 300 a hectare a year.
Futures for the 2028 harvest trade at about Th 228.
